_purpose: Knobs for Module CURATOR. Periodically (manual trigger today, cron later) the Curator scans accumulated USER.md / MEMORY.md / SKILL.md and emits proposals for consolidating duplicates, archiving stale skills, and refining wording. ALL proposals route through 105 approval — nothing auto-applies. This is the Hermes-style 'LLM reviews LLM' layer, but with the governance shield Hermes does not have.

scope._doc: Which surfaces does the curator review. Separate scope per surface so user can disable individual ones (e.g. SKILL.md curation but no USER.md curation).

proposal_limits._doc: Hard caps per run. The first run on a populated memory will propose a lot — the cap keeps the human review queue manageable. The 105 approval card UI shows them one at a time.

staleness._doc: Skills unused for N days are AUTO-PROPOSED for archive (proposal still needs human approval, just nominated automatically). USER.md / MEMORY.md entries have no staleness concept — only the LLM judges relevance during review.

forbidden_patterns._doc: Regex patterns (case-insensitive) that cause the curator's proposed NEW_TEXT to be REJECTED at apply time even if a human approved it (defense in depth — same defense as reflection_constraints + skill_constraints). Catches the case where the curator LLM gets prompt-injected into proposing a malicious rewrite of USER.md.

llm_call._doc: Per-scope LLM call config. The curator calls the chat LLM once per scope (USER.md / MEMORY.md / skills list) so each scope gets independent JSON output and a fresh context budget.
